title: Russia evasive after the US says Europe will join next Ukraine talks | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

Russia remained evasive on Friday after US negotiators said that European delegates would join the next round of peace talks with Ukraine.

Aftera day of diplomacysaw US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner meet both Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Russia’s President Vladimir Putin, Kushner posted on X that “both sides” agreed to a European presence, something long sought by both Kyiv and leaders on the continent. While in Russia, Witkoff told CNN the move was “a very big deal.”

But the Kremlin has since responded cooly, neither explicitly endorsing a European delegation nor flatly rejecting it.

“Putin has never refused to engage with the Europeans,” the Kremlin’s spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, told journalists on Friday. “If the Europeans truly have someone who is authorized to hold discussions … then, of course, we would be prepared to talk with them.”

“Once we understand their actual intentions and their willingness to contribute to the peace process, we can then make a decision regarding a dialogue in an expanded format,” he added.

On Friday, the President of the European Council António Costa said the European team would be represented by the EU institutions and the E5 nations of France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the UK.

“Our European team will continue to act in full unity and in close coordination with all member states,” Costa said.

Earlier, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz underlined Europe’s position in a pointed message to the US.

“Please, no surprises. Keep playing as part of Team Europe and as part of the team with Ukraine, and let us work together for a genuine peace in Ukraine,” he said.

Meanwhile, Kyiv’s forces on the ground were unable to fend off concurrent Russian salvos. That followed repeated disruptions to Starshield – a military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink service critical to Ukraine’s military operations.

Zelensky told reporters in Dublin the recent discussions gave Kyiv “hope that we will end this war.”

Speaking alongside Witkoff and Kushner on Thursday night, Zelensky also said that a recently agreed prisoner of war exchange would be the biggest since the start of the war, calling the swap “a real result.”

Earlier, just before the US envoys departed Moscow, Witkoff told CNN’s Frederik Pleitgen at Vnukovo Airport: “I think progress was made. I think it was made earlier today. People didn’t think that we were going to restart trilateral. We’ve restarted it. We’ve set a new meeting.”

“This is what President (Donald) Trump wants to see,” he added.

“This will allow us to address the broader postwar European security agreements alongside the territorial issues between Ukraine and Russia,” Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law who acts as one of the country’s top diplomats despite holding no official role within the administration,posted on Xon Thursday.

Putin claimed that Moscow had “never been opposed to engaging in dialogue with Europe.” “We have never broken it off,” he said in the meeting with both White House envoys.

“We are aware that territorial issues are viewed differently by the two sides,” Putin said. “This, as I have already said, will always be a bone of contention,” he added.

While Ukraine has long argued that Europe should be at the main negotiating table, Moscow has previously resisted such efforts.

Earlier this week, Putin’s foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov – while confirming that trilateral talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the US would continue – appeared to play down the suggestion that European representatives would join them, hinting “they need to decide whether they want peace or a continuation of the war.”

Asked if Russia was suspicious of Europe’s intentions, Russian presidential special envoy Kirill Dmitriev told CNN Thursday: “I think working on European security is definitely a great, important step for Europe. And frankly, people who care about Europeans and their lives, of course, want European security to be strong.”

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov also criticized the presence of European officials in the UAE city earlier this week, saying their involvement was not a “promising approach.”

Meanwhile, Ushakov said Putin and Trump will “continue discussions” about Ukraine during a planned bilateral meeting at the APEC summit in China.

Before the meeting with the US envoys, Zelensky joined other world leaders in Dublin earlier on Thursday for the European Political Community summit, where the discussions in Abu Dhabi were discussed, as well as additional sanctions on Russia.

Despite the flurry of diplomacy, the latest push for peace has not afforded Ukraine respite from the daily barrage of Russian attacks.

Ukrainian troops stationed on the front line and in occupied areas were still facing Starshield speed issues on Friday, according to Zelensky, citing limits of 161 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour). The Ukrainian leader said he’d told officials to contact the US State Department, the Pentagon and SpaceX “to obtain clarification and resolve the situation.”

The White House, the US State Department and the Pentagon did not response to CNN’s request for comment. SpaceX, the company which owns Starshield, previously told CNN that there had been no change in its service.

In October too, Ukraine said speed limits were imposed on Starshield satellite terminals, as the relationship between Kyiv and Washington deteriorated. Trump denied approving that decision, while Musk said the Trump administration was behind the restrictions.

At least 10 people were killed and 48 others injured in Ukraine Thursday into Friday, according to regional officials.

In Russia, air defenses intercepted and downed nearly 1,198 Ukrainian drones overnight into Friday, according to the Russian defense ministry. At least eight people were killed in those strikes, according to a CNN tally of figures released by local governors.

It came after Ukraine’s Armed Forces said the military hit Russian drone production and repair sites in the southwestern city of Rostov-on-Don on Friday.

CNN’s Svitlana Vlasova, Katharina Krebs and Anna Chernova contributed reporting.

CNN’s Svitlana Vlasova, Katharina Krebs and Anna Chernova contributed reporting.
